# Engine tool reference

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_docs.py - do not edit -->

The engine exposes **186 tools** (the same table the PdfCraft CLI / MCP server use). Each is available three ways:

```python
pdf.<tool>("in.pdf", ..., out=None)          # one call, path based   (pypdfcraft.oneshot)
pdf.apply("in.pdf", "<tool>", ..., out=None)  # same, by name
doc.<tool>(...)  /  doc.<group>.<name>(...)   # on an open Document (document id filled in)
```

Pages are **1-based**.

## `accessibility_autotag_apply`

**Automatically tag text-only PDF**

Write marked content, a Document structure element, paragraph tags and a parent tree for every text object in an untagged, text-only PDF. Refuses graphics, images, annotations, forms, existing tags and malformed streams before changing anything. Review all resulting roles; this does not certify accessibility. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |

## `accessibility_autotag_form_fields`

**Tag form fields**

Write `/Form` tags, widget structure-parent keys, and a parent tree for all page widgets in an untagged AcroForm. Existing tag trees are refused for review. Text, figures, links, and other content are not tagged.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |

## `accessibility_autotag_preview`

**Preview automatic tags**  _(read-only)_

Propose paragraph and heading tags for visible text blocks on one page. Returns page bounds, tentative roles and reasons. Does not change the PDF or claim accessibility compliance. Images, tables, lists, annotations and existing structure require separate review.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `page` * | integer |  |

## `accessibility_check`

**Check for accessibility**  _(read-only)_

Run the Accessibility Checker's full check (32 rules in 7 categories: document, page_content, forms, alternate_text, tables, lists, headings). Each rule is passed, failed (with findings and pages), manual (needs a person) or skipped. Findings on locatable figures, annotations and form widgets include bbox_user_space in PDF coordinates. Colour contrast is off unless all is true; rules (ids such as tagged-pdf, figures-alt-text) or categories narrow the check; pages limit the page rules.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `all` | boolean | Include rules that are off by default (colour contrast). |
| `categories` | array |  |
| `pages` | array | 1-based page numbers for the page rules (default: all). |
| `rules` | array |  |

## `accessibility_figures`

**List figures**  _(read-only)_

The tagged figures (Figure elements, through the role map) in document order: figure number, page, alternate text and where the figure is drawn (top-left-origin points).

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |

## `accessibility_find_untagged`

**Find untagged content**  _(read-only)_

Find untagged painted page content, annotations, and form widgets. This focused check does not modify the PDF or claim that its other accessibility rules pass.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `pages` | array | 1-based page numbers to search (default: all). |

## `accessibility_fix`

**Fix an accessibility problem**

Apply the checker's automatic fix for a rule: primary-language (value: the language, e.g. en-US), title (value: the title; default the current title or file name; also shows it in the title bar) or tab-order (every page tabs in structure order). Returns the rule's new status. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `rule` * | enum: primary-language, title, tab-order |  |
| `value` | string |  |

## `accessibility_mark_tag_artifact`

**Mark tag content as artifact**

Mark a reachable leaf structure tag's direct marked content as an artifact and remove the tag from the reading structure. Use object and generation from accessibility_tags. Tags with child structure elements, no direct marked content, or content not found on its page are rejected. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `generation` * | integer |  |
| `object` * | integer |  |

## `accessibility_move_tag`

**Move structure tag**

Move a reachable indirect structure tag before or after a direct sibling in their parent's /K array, changing tagged reading order without changing page appearance. Use object and generation values from accessibility_tags. Rejects distinct parents, duplicate references and positions that are already current. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `anchor` * | integer |  |
| `anchor_generation` * | integer |  |
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `generation` * | integer |  |
| `object` * | integer |  |
| `placement` * | enum: before, after |  |

**Accessibility review summary**

Compare two open versions of a PDF and write a self-contained HTML summary of the same evidence as accessibility_review_record: document hashes, outcome counts, rule changes, and rules still requiring review. Does not change either PDF or claim accessibility compliance.

|---|---|---|
| `after` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `before` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | string |  |
| `all` | boolean | Include rules that are off by default (colour contrast). |

**Open accessibility review decisions**  _(read-only)_

Read a local review sidecar only when its recorded SHA-256 matches the open PDF. Returns the decisions without changing the PDF.

| argument | type | |

| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | string |  |

## `accessibility_review_record`

**Accessibility review record**

Compare the same accessibility rules on two open versions of a PDF and write a JSON record to path. Includes document SHA-256 hashes, before/after rule statuses and finding counts, changed rules, and rules still needing review. Does not change either PDF or claim accessibility compliance. Open the original and edited copies as separate documents.

| argument | type | |

| `after` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `before` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | string |  |
| `all` | boolean | Include rules that are off by default (colour contrast). |

## `accessibility_review_save`

**Save accessibility review decisions**

Write a local JSON sidecar for an open PDF with rule-level human review decisions. The sidecar records the PDF SHA-256; replacing one tied to different bytes requires replace: true. Does not change the PDF or assert compliance.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `decisions` * | array |  |
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | string |  |
| `replace` | boolean |  |

Set a figure's alternate text (alt; empty or omitted clears it), or mark it decorative (decorative: true: its content becomes an artifact and the figure leaves the tags). figure is a number from accessibility_figures. Returns the figures. Undoable.

| argument | type | |

## `accessibility_set_tag_property`

**Edit tag property**

Set or clear one property of a reachable indirect structure tag. Use object and generation from accessibility_tags. Properties: type, title, actual_text, alternate_text, language, summary (Table tags: the table's Summary attribute), scope (TH tags: Row, Column or Both). Summary and scope are written in the tag's Table attribute object (/A, /O /Table); the role map decides a tag's type. Empty or omitted value clears text properties, summary and scope; type requires a nonempty PDF name. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `generation` * | integer |  |
| `object` * | integer |  |
| `property` * | enum: type, title, actual_text, alternate_text, language, summary, scope |  |
| `value` | string |  |

## `accessibility_tags`

**List structure tags**  _(read-only)_

List reachable indirect structure tags in document order with PDF object number, generation, nearest indirect parent, depth, page, type, title, actual text, alternate text, language, a table's summary and a header cell's scope, one page at a time: count is how many tags match, next the offset of the following page (null at the end). types, pages and max_depth keep only some tags. Inline tag dictionaries have no stable object reference and are not listed.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `limit` | integer | Tags in the page (default 200) |
| `max_depth` | integer | Only tags at most this deep (0 = top level) |
| `offset` | integer | Where the page starts, counted from 0 (the previous page's next) |
| `pages` | array | Only tags on these pages |
| `types` | array | Only tags of these types, as listed in type (such as H1, H2, Table) |

## `bookmark_add`

**Add a bookmark**

Add a bookmark that goes to a page, under a parent bookmark (or at the top level), at a position. It goes to the top of the page, or to a place on it: `top` and `left` are points from the top-left of the displayed page (like the destination bookmark_list reports), each optional, and a coordinate left out keeps the reader's position that way. The zoom is kept. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `page` * | integer |  |
| `title` * | string |  |
| `left` | number | Points from the left of the displayed page. |
| `parent` | array | Parent bookmark (omit for the top level): 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark. |
| `position` | integer | 1-based position among the parent's children (default: last). |
| `top` | number | Points from the top of the displayed page. |

## `bookmark_delete`

**Delete a bookmark**

Delete a bookmark and the bookmarks under it. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | array | The bookmark: 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark. |

## `bookmark_from_structure`

**New bookmarks from structure**

Make bookmarks from the document's tagged headings (H, H1-H6), nested by level under a new first bookmark titled "Untitled". Fails if the document has no tagged headings. Returns the first page of the bookmark tree (see bookmark_list). Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |

## `bookmark_from_text_styles`

**New bookmarks from text styles**

Make bookmarks from the lines set in chosen text styles, for documents whose headings are not tagged: levels lists one style per bookmark level ({font, size, bold, italic} as text_styles gives them; sizes within a quarter point match), the first level 1, the next nested under the bookmark before it, and so on. A heading set on several lines is one bookmark, and each goes to the top of its heading. They go under a new first bookmark titled "Untitled". Fails if no text is set in the styles. Returns the first page of the bookmark tree (see bookmark_list). Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `levels` * | array |  |

## `bookmark_list`

**List bookmarks**  _(read-only)_

The bookmarks in outline order, one page at a time: each with its path (1-based, as the other bookmark tools take it), title, target page and open state, its colour ([r, g, b], 0-1) and bold or italic style when it has them, and its children on the same page. next is the offset of the following page, or null at the end. Bookmarks nested deeper than 33 levels are not listed.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `limit` | integer | Bookmarks in the page (default 100) |
| `offset` | integer | Where the page starts, counted from 0 (the previous page's next) |

## `comment_add`

**Add a comment**

Add a comment as Acrobat's commenting tools do. Geometry is in points with the origin at the top-left of the displayed page, y down (as in page_render images at 72 dpi and text_find rects). note: `at` [x, y] (icon top-left). stamp: `at` [x, y] (its centre) and `stamp`: approved, completed, confidential, draft, final, for comment, for public release, information only, not approved, not for public release, preliminary results, void, accepted, initial here, rejected, sign here, witness; dynamic: true for the dynamic approved/confidential/received/reviewed/revised stamps with a By … at … line. highlight/underline/strikeout/squiggly: `find` (text on the page to mark; every match with all: true) or `quads`. rectangle/oval/textbox: `rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1]. line/arrow: `from`, `to`. Optional `endings` (two names: start, end) for a line, arrow or polyline, or one name for a callout: None, Square, Circle, Diamond, OpenArrow, ClosedArrow, Butt, ROpenArrow, RClosedArrow, Slash. An arrow without endings is None then OpenArrow. ink: `strokes` [[[x, y], …], …]. polygon/cloud/polyline (connected lines): `points` [[x, y], …]. callout: `rect` (its text box), `to` (the point the arrow touches), optional `knee`. caret (inserted text): `at`, the insertion point on the baseline. replace (Replace Text): `find` or `quads` like highlight, `contents` the replacement. attachment: `path` (the file), `at`, optional `icon` (PushPin, Paperclip, Graph, Tag). sound (a voice comment): `path` (a 16-bit PCM .wav recording, mono or stereo), `at`. Undoable. Text a text box, callout or stamp draws in the standard fonts that they can't draw (Chinese, Greek) is saved as typed and drawn as `?`; `warnings` in the result says so.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `page` * | integer |  |
| `type` * | enum: note, highlight, underline, strikeout, squiggly, replace, rectangle, oval, line, arrow, ink, freehand_highlight, textbox, stamp, polygon, cloud, polyline, callout, caret, attachment, sound |  |
| `all` | boolean | Mark every match of `find` on the page, not just the first. |
| `at` | array | [x, y] in points from the top-left of the displayed page. |
| `author` | string |  |
| `color` | string | #RRGGBB or a name: yellow, red, orange, green, blue, purple, pink, black, gray, white. |
| `contents` | string | The comment text (what a text box shows). |
| `dynamic` | boolean |  |
| `endings` | array | Line endings. Two names (start, end) for a line, arrow or polyline; one name for a callout. |
| `fill` | string | #RRGGBB or a name: yellow, red, orange, green, blue, purple, pink, black, gray, white. |
| `find` | string | Text on the page to mark up (case-insensitive). |
| `font_size` | number |  |
| `from` | array | [x, y] in points from the top-left of the displayed page. |
| `icon` | string | note: Comment, Note, Help, Insert, Key, NewParagraph, Paragraph (the standard names), Check, Circle, Cross, CrossHairs, Star, RightArrow, UpArrow; attachment: PushPin, Paperclip, Graph, Tag. |
| `knee` | array | [x, y] in points from the top-left of the displayed page. |
| `opacity` | number |  |
| `path` | string | attachment: the file to attach; sound: the .wav recording. |
| `points` | array |  |
| `quads` | array |  |
| `rect` | array |  |
| `stamp` | string |  |
| `strokes` | array |  |
| `to` | array | [x, y] in points from the top-left of the displayed page. |
| `width` | number | Line width in points. |

## `comment_delete`

**Delete a comment**

Delete a comment with its pop-up and replies, or one reply (its id, or page and index, from comment_list) with its pop-up and the replies to it; the comment and its other replies stay. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `id` | string | The comment's id (from comment_list). An id several comments share is refused: pass page and index. |
| `index` | integer | 1-based position on the page, as comment_list reports. |
| `page` | integer | With `index`, instead of `id`. |

## `comment_edit`

**Edit a comment**

Change a comment's text, colour, opacity, line width, font size (text box/typewriter/callout), fill (rectangle/oval/polygon/text box/callout; "none" removes it), rectangle (rectangle/oval/text box/stamp), position (`move` [dx, dy] in points) or shape (`points`: a line's two ends, or the corners of connected lines, a polygon or a cloud). Stamps keep their original appearance when resized. One undo step.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `color` | string | #RRGGBB or a name: yellow, red, orange, green, blue, purple, pink, black, gray, white. |
| `contents` | string |  |
| `fill` | string | Interior colour of a rectangle, oval, polygon, text box or callout: #RRGGBB, a colour name, or "none" for no fill. |
| `font_size` | number | Font size in points of a text box, typewriter text or callout; the box grows to hold the text. |
| `id` | string | The comment's id (from comment_list). An id several comments share is refused: pass page and index. |
| `index` | integer | 1-based position on the page, as comment_list reports. |
| `move` | array | [x, y] in points from the top-left of the displayed page. |
| `opacity` | number |  |
| `page` | integer | With `index`, instead of `id`. |
| `points` | array | A line's two ends, or every corner of connected lines, a polygon or a cloud, in page coordinates. |
| `rect` | array |  |
| `width` | number |  |

## `comment_erase`

**Erase part of drawings**

The Eraser: rub out the parts of the drawings (ink comments) on a page within radius points of path, splitting strokes where the path cuts them. A drawing with nothing left is deleted, a locked one is left alone. One undoable step, as the Eraser in PdfCraft; returns how many drawings the path came near (0: nothing changed).

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `page` * | integer |  |
| `path` * | array | The eraser's path: [x, y] points from the top-left of the page. |
| `radius` | number | How far from the path it erases, in points. Default 6. |

## `comment_image_preview`

**Preview image signature layers**  _(read-only)_

Return a PNG of the page without the selected image signature/initials (layer=background, default), or its embedded image with alpha (layer=image). Includes the displayed rectangle, document rotation, image_rotation (how far clockwise the image is shown turned) and annotation opacity. Cache these layers for live placement/resizing; commit once with comment_edit. Does not change the document or undo history.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `dpi` | number |  |
| `id` | string | The comment's id (from comment_list). An id several comments share is refused: pass page and index. |
| `index` | integer | 1-based position on the page, as comment_list reports. |
| `layer` | enum: background, image |  |
| `page` | integer | With `index`, instead of `id`. |

## `doc_audit_redactions`

Find faux redactions: opaque filled rectangles painted over text that is still extractable, and /Redact annotations that were marked but never applied. ## `doc_batch`

**Process files and folders**

Run convert, ocr and/or optimize over files and folders, one file at a time. recursive defaults to false. Preserve paths relative to each selected folder inside out_dir; duplicate inputs run once. Skip unsupported files, links and the output subtree. Existing outputs receive numbered names and are never replaced. Continue after per-file errors unless stop_on_error is true. Return completed/failed/skipped counts and per-file results. Discovery is bounded to 10000 entries and 64 folder levels. Convert must be first; each step can appear once. OCR uses installed models. Optimize uses Reduce File Size settings, optionally overriding target ppi (threshold 1.5 times ppi; black-and-white images go to the larger of ppi and 300) and JPEG quality; a larger candidate keeps the original bytes. Sources and open documents are unchanged.

| `quality` | integer |  |
| `recursive` | boolean |  |
| `skip_text_pages` | boolean |  |
| `stop_on_error` | boolean |  |

## `doc_combine`

**Combine files**

Combine files, in order, into one PDF (bookmarks are kept under one entry per file). Images (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF, BMP, JPEG 2000), .txt files and Word/Excel/PowerPoint/RTF documents (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .rtf) are made into PDFs first. pages optionally chooses each file's pages, in step with paths: a range such as "1-3, 6" or null for all pages. passwords, also in step with paths, opens encrypted files (the open password, or the permissions password where a file's security doesn't allow copying pages; null for none). The result is not encrypted. Passwords are never echoed back. groups, also in step with paths, splits a file around others: entries with the same number (they must name the same path) are one file, copied once, so it keeps one bookmark at its first page, its links and its form fields; null for a file of its own. A group uses its first entry's password. When two files' forms name the same field, field_conflicts says what happens: "rename" (the default) keeps the fields separate by renaming the later one (Text1 becomes Text1-1) and the result lists renamed_fields as [[old, new], …] — scripts that refer to the old name are not rewritten; "merge" makes them one field, as before.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` * | array |  |
| `field_conflicts` | enum: rename, merge |  |
| `groups` | array |  |
| `open` | boolean | Also open the result as a new document (default: only when out is omitted). |
| `out` | string | File to write. Omit to open the result as a new unsaved document instead. |
| `pages` | array |  |
| `passwords` | array |  |

## `doc_export_office`

**Export to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML, RTF or Markdown**

Export a PDF ▸ Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), HTML (.html, one file with images inline), RTF (.rtf) or Markdown (.md or .markdown: pipe tables, images left out), chosen by path's extension: text, headings, bold and italic. HTML uses rich styling by default; set html_mode to simple for CSS-free headings, paragraphs, emphasis and tables. Simple HTML keeps text and inline images but omits colour and layout styling. Word uses borderless inferred tables and positioned editable shapes on pages with artwork, rotated or large text; each source page retains its size. Excel writes one worksheet per page: detected tables as cell grids (spanning cells merged, plain numbers as numbers), other paragraphs one per row in column A; images are left out. PowerPoint writes one slide per page (sized like the first page) with each paragraph as a text box, each image as a picture and each detected table as a table, at their page positions. Font matching and vector graphics remain limited. Export reads forms 50 deep and up to 50 000 a page, counting forms the page draws itself. Pages that go past either limit, or that have pictures past what one export may hold or decode, are listed in truncated_pages, with a warning; what was left out is missing.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | string |  |
| `html_mode` | enum: rich, simple |  |

## `doc_optimize`

**Optimize PDF**

Write an optimized copy to `path` (Acrobat's PDF Optimizer). preset: standard (default; Reduce File Size's choices) or mobile (images to 96 ppi above 144, JPEG high quality); the options below change it. compatibility: retain (default; keeps the document's version, or 1.5 when object streams are written), 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7 or 2.0. merge_fragments (default true) first puts a page picture drawn as many stacked image strips (as some PDF printers write it) back together into one image, so it can be resampled (merged_images, fragments_merged). color / gray: { downsample, ppi, above_ppi, compression: jpeg|zip|retain, quality 1–100 } (defaults: downsample to 150 ppi above 225, JPEG 60). mono: { downsample, ppi, above_ppi, compression: ccitt_g4|jbig2|retain } for black-and-white images and image masks (default: averaged down to 300 ppi above 450 ppi, counted in images_resampled; stored losslessly as CCITT Group 4 or JBIG2 (or 1-bit Flate, once resampled or packed from more bits) when that is smaller, Group 3 fax images, JBIG2 images, black-and-white RGB and indexed images using only palette entries 0 and 1 among them, counted in images_recompressed; retain resamples only, a CCITT image staying CCITT, a JBIG2 image JBIG2 and any other becoming Flate). Images past what one run may decode stay as they are, counted in images_refused; streams it only stores with Flate past that stay LZW, uncounted. Images are measured where pages draw them and replaced only when smaller. discard_*: thumbnails (default true), alternate_images (true), tags, print_settings; flate_unencoded (true); object_streams (default true; always off for 1.4); lzw_to_flate (true) decodes LZW streams and stores them with Flate instead, leaving any it cannot decode unchanged (lzw_streams counts the streams converted); remove_invalid_links and remove_unreferenced_dests (true); images and forms the pages list but never draw are always dropped (unused_xobjects). discard: Remove Hidden Information categories (metadata, attachments, comments, form-fields, hidden-text, hidden-layers, bookmarks, links-actions-scripts, private-data). Signed documents are refused. The open document is unchanged.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | string |  |
| `color` | object |  |
| `compatibility` | enum: retain, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 2.0 |  |
| `discard` | array |  |

## `doc_protect`

**Protect with passwords**

Encrypt the document (applied by the next doc_save, a full rewrite). open_password is needed to open it. permissions_password is needed to change security and lifts the restrictions given by printing/changes/copy/accessibility; those restrictions (and their defaults) apply only when permissions_password is given. With open_password alone the document is encrypted and everything stays allowed, so passing a restriction without permissions_password is an error. Passwords are never echoed back. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `accessibility` | boolean | Allow screen readers to read the text (needs permissions_password; default true). |
| `changes` | enum: none, pages, fill-sign, comment-fill-sign, any-except-extract | Needs permissions_password. Default none. |
| `compatibility` | enum: aes-256, aes-128, rc4-128, rc4-40 | Default aes-256 (Acrobat X and later). |
| `copy` | boolean | Allow copying text and images (needs permissions_password; default false). |
| `encrypt_metadata` | boolean | Default true. |
| `open_password` | string | Required to open the document. On its own it restricts nothing. |
| `permissions_password` | string | Required to change security; enables printing/changes/copy/accessibility and their defaults. |
| `printing` | enum: none, low, high | Needs permissions_password. Default high. |

## `doc_reduce`

**Reduce file size**

Write a smaller copy of the document to `path` with Acrobat's Reduce File Size choices: colour and grey images above 225 ppi downsampled to 150 ppi and JPEG-compressed (medium quality), black-and-white images averaged down to 300 ppi above 450 ppi and each stored as CCITT Group 4 (or 1-bit Flate, once resampled or packed from more bits) whenever that is smaller, thumbnails dropped, identical fonts and images merged, unused objects dropped, compressed object streams. If the copy wouldn't be smaller, nothing is written and `written` is false. Images past what one run may decode stay as they are, counted in images_refused; streams it only stores with Flate past that stay LZW, uncounted. The open document is unchanged.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `path` * | string |  |

## `fill_sign_add`

**Fill & Sign: type text or place a mark**

Fill in a form that has no fields, as Acrobat's Fill & Sign does: type text (`text`, default 10 pt; `font_size` 4–300 pt; optional `color` as #RRGGBB for text/date, default black), place a check, cross, dot or line, today's date (in Preferences ▸ Date format, see fill_sign_date_format, or `format`; `font_size` also applies), or a signature or initials (either `text` drawn in a script font, or `path` to a local PNG/JPEG image up to 4 MiB and 32 megapixels, scaled down to 4 megapixels, preserving transparency; with `scan: true`, `path` is instead a photo of a signature on paper, within the same limits: the signature is found, and the paper, shadows and table around it are removed, with `sensitivity` 0–100, default 50, picking up fainter ink when higher). `at` [x, y] is in points from the top-left of the page: text's top-left, mark's centre, signature's left edge centred vertically. Image signatures fit within 150 pt wide and 32 pt tall (24 pt for initials). Creates movable, undoable annotations. Typed text the standard fonts can't draw is saved and drawn as `?` (`warnings` in the result says so); a typed signature neither the script font nor its fallback can draw is refused (pass `path` instead).

|---|---|---|

| `format` | string | For type date: this pattern instead of the date-format preference, e.g. "dd.mm.yyyy". |
| `language` | string | For type date: month and weekday names in this language code (see fill_sign_date_format) instead of the preference. |
| `path` | string | PNG or JPEG for signature/initials; pass either path or text. |
| `scan` | boolean | With path: scan a photo of a signature on paper (default false). |
| `sensitivity` | integer | With scan: how faint ink may be, 0–100 (default 50). |
| `text` | string |  |

## `fill_sign_date_format`

**Date format for Fill & Sign**

Preferences ▸ Date format: the pattern Fill & Sign dates use (default m/d/yyyy). Set it with `format` (Acrobat date codes yyyy yy mmmm mmm mm m dddd ddd dd d, other runs of y, m or d are refused; H h M s t are time letters and need \ before them; \ shows the next character as is), or read it. `language` sets the language of month and weekday names (a code from `languages`, or `auto` to follow the app's interface language; English headless). Returns the format, the language, today in them, `unwritable` (characters of today's date that Fill & Sign can't write into a PDF yet, Western European only; fill_sign_add refuses such a date), the ready-made presets and the languages.

| `language` | string |  |

## `form_add_field_table`

**Prepare form: add a table of text fields**

Divide rect into rows and columns of text fields, one per cell, as one undo step. rect in points from the top-left of the displayed page [x0, y0, x1, y1]; rows 1-100 from the top; columns 1-50, or as many as names or widths list. Each column names its cells from its pattern in names: an N on its own after _ - / or : (price_N), # or {row} is the row number, {col} the column number, {seq} counts every cell along the rows, starting at first_row; with none of them the row number goes at the end. Rows count from first_row (default 1). Without names the columns are Table1_N, Table1_c2_N, … using the first free TableK. widths are relative (default equal); row_gap and column_gap are points between cells (default 0). Nothing is added if a cell would be under 4 points or a name would contain a period, repeat, or already exist; the error says which. Returns the fields' names. Undoable.

## `form_calculation_order`

**Read or set the calculation order**

The calculated fields in the order they calculate (Acrobat: Set Field Calculation Order), each with its `formula` (as form_fields shows calculate), the fields it reads (`reads`; a script's names built at run time aren't known) and its `issues`: missing_field (it reads `field`, which the form doesn't have, so it gets no value there), runs_too_early (it reads `field`, which calculates after it, so it shows a stale value), cycle (it reads `fields`, which read it back: no order fixes that, a formula has to change) and not_in_order (the PDF's order leaves it out, so other viewers may not calculate it) and built_names (its script also reads fields by names it builds at run time, which aren't checked). `extra` lists entries of the PDF's order that calculate nothing. Without a change it only reads. Changes, one at a time: `order` (these fields first, in this order, then the other calculated fields in their order), `field` with `move` earlier|later (one place), or `fix` true (only what must move moves, so every field calculates after the fields it reads, and the extra entries go). A change recalculates the form. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `field` | string |  |
| `fix` | boolean |  |
| `move` | enum: earlier, later |  |
| `order` | array |  |

## `form_set_props`

**Field properties**

Change field properties: give field for one field, or fields for a list of unique field names (1–1000). A bulk change is atomic and one Undo step; an invalid or locked field leaves every field unchanged. Only the given properties change, and partial appearance changes preserve each field's other colours and font. name (rename: a dotted name such as MASTER.first is the full name and moves the field under those parent fields; a plain name renames it within its parent), rect (position), rotation and caption require a single field. A rename also renames the field in the calculations that read it (calculate field lists and notation, and getField calls naming it in a string literal; names built at run time are not rewritten), in the same Undo step, and formulas_updated lists the fields whose calculation changed. caption changes one push-button normal label (widget: 1-based index, default 1); an empty string clears it. Other widgets and icon-only layouts are preserved. General and Options: tooltip, read_only, required, multiline, max_length (0 = no limit), options (combo/list items), font_size (0 = auto), format, validate, calculate (Acrobat's native AF rules). Options: align (left, center, right), default (Reset form's value; check boxes/radio buttons use their on state, "" for off), flags { scroll, rich_text, password, file_select, spell_check, comb (needs max_length), sort, editable, multi_select, commit_immediately }, check_style (check boxes/radio buttons: check, circle, cross, diamond, square, star). rotation is 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees counterclockwise and swaps width/height when the axis changes. Returns the resulting order of fields (`tab_order`) and each page's tab order (`page_tabs`, as Page properties ▸ Tab Order shows it). Undoable.

| argument | type | |

## `image_edit`

**Edit an image**

Change one of a page's images (number from page_images): action move (rect: new full placement box in top-left-origin points, based on page_images.rect), crop (rect: the part to keep, top-left-origin points; the pixels stay in place and page_images.visible_rect shows the result; a later move carries the crop along), remove_crop (remove a crop created by PdfCraft while preserving clipping paths from the original document), rotate (quarters clockwise, default 1), rotate_by (degrees: any angle clockwise about the visible centre; the box in page_images then becomes the turned image's bounding box), transform (matrix: 6 numbers [a, b, c, d, e, f] in top-left-origin points, applied after the current placement so a point (x, y) of the image moves to (a·x + c·y + e, b·x + d·y + f); finite, with a·d − b·c not 0; the box in page_images becomes the transformed image's bounding box), flip_horizontal (reflect left/right on the displayed page), flip_vertical (reflect top/bottom on the displayed page; both flip actions follow the page rotation), replace (path: an image file, drawn in the same place), delete, or arrange: bring_to_front, send_to_back, bring_forward, send_backward (reorder stacking order among content on the page; errors when the image is already at the requested limit; arranging an added image converts it into an ordinary page image). Undoable. The selected image crop transforms with its pixels, isolating shared path scopes while retaining neighboring painting. Text-outline clips return a clear error. Rotation/flip use the visible centre. Form artwork supports move/resize/rotate/flip/delete as a group; replace and image_save only support raster images.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `action` * | enum: move, crop, rotate, rotate_by, transform, flip_horizontal, flip_vertical, replace, delete, bring_to_front, send_to_back, bring_forward, send_backward, remove_crop |  |
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `image` * | integer |  |
| `page` * | integer |  |
| `degrees` | number |  |
| `matrix` | array |  |
| `path` | string |  |
| `quarters` | integer |  |
| `rect` | array |  |

## `ocr_recognize`

**Recognize text (OCR)**

Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text: render pages, read the words in them and add them as invisible text over the page image, so scanned pages become searchable and selectable (a searchable image; the image is not changed). Pages that already have text are skipped unless skip_text_pages is false; then pictures on those pages are read too, and recognised words that the page's own text already has (an earlier OCR layer included) are left out and counted as already_on_page. Returns each page's recognised text (left out when the document's security doesn't allow copying), word count or why it was skipped. Needs the OCR models (ocr_status). Undoable as one step.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `dpi` | number | Resolution pages are read at (default 300; a scanned page is read at most at its own resolution). |
| `language` | enum: en | Document language (default en). |
| `pages` | array | 1-based page numbers to recognise (default: all). |
| `skip_text_pages` | boolean | Leave pages that already contain text alone (default true). false also reads pictures on such pages, without adding their text again. |

## `ocr_recognize_files`

**Recognize text in multiple files**

Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text ▸ In multiple files: read every page of each PDF in paths and write the searchable result into folder under the same name (pages that already have text are left alone unless skip_text_pages is false, as in ocr_recognize). Two inputs that would write the same output file are refused before anything is read or written. Returns, per file, the output path, word count and skipped pages, or the error.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` * | string |  |
| `paths` * | array |  |
| `dpi` | number |  |
| `language` | enum: en |  |
| `skip_text_pages` | boolean | Leave pages that already contain text alone (default true); see ocr_recognize. |

## `page_enhance_camera`

**Enhance camera image**

Straighten a photographed document (Scan & OCR ▸ Enhance ▸ Camera image): the part of the page inside the four corners (x1, y1, … x4, y4 in top-left-origin points, any order, a convex quadrilateral; when omitted, the document's edges are found automatically, or an error says they could not be) is warped to an upright rectangle that replaces what the page shows, at the page picture's own resolution (at most 600 dpi). mode is how it looks: original, colour (default), greyscale or bw (black and white, stored losslessly). level (0–100, default 0) then cleans the photo up: even lighting so the paper turns white (casts, shadows, dark edges), more contrast, and from 60 no isolated specks; colour ink stays colour. For bw the level is the threshold (higher keeps fainter strokes black). The page's comments, links and bookmarks stay. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `page` * | integer |  |
| `corners` | array |  |
| `level` | integer |  |
| `mode` | enum: original, colour, greyscale, bw |  |

## `redact_mark`

**Mark for redaction**

Mark content for redaction (nothing is removed until redact_apply). One of: rect [x0, y0, x1, y1] (points from the top-left of the displayed page) with page; find (text, every match); words (a list of words or phrases, every match of each; the result's matched_words says how many marks each made); pattern (phone, email, credit-card, ssn, date: every match, Acrobat's Search & Redact patterns); whole_pages: true. find and words accept case_sensitive and whole_words (both default false). Select one page with page or multiple with pages (default all); do not pass both. rect requires page. overlay: text shown on the box once applied, or code_set (foia: U.S. FOIA (b)(1)(A)…(b)(9); privacy-act: U.S. Privacy Act (d)(5), (j)(1)…(k)(7)) with codes, shown as "(b)(6), (b)(7)(C)"; fill: box colour (default black). Undoable.

## `sign_document`

**Sign a document**

Sign with a digital ID (a .p12/.pfx path, or on macOS a Keychain identity: "keychain:<common name or fingerprint>" from sign_keychain_ids, or on Windows a store identity: "windows:<common name or fingerprint>" from sign_windows_ids) and save the signed file to `out` (signing always saves, as in Acrobat; the document then shows the signed file). Sign an existing empty signature field (`field`), or a new one on `page` at `rect` (omit rect for an invisible signature). certify: no_changes, form_fill or comments makes a certification signature. graphic shows a picture where the signer's name would be large (Acrobat: Configure Signature Appearance): {"image": path} (PNG or JPEG), {"text": name} (typed in the Fill & Sign script font) or {"strokes": [[[x, y], …], …]} (y up, the drawing pad 1 wide); it needs a visible signature. appearance chooses what a visible signature shows (default: name, date and labels; reason, location and distinguished_name are off unless turned on). labels gives the words of its labels, e.g. in another language (default English: "Digitally signed by", "DN: ", "Reason: ", "Location: ", "Date: "; include the separator); each must be in Western European characters (Windows-1252), the only ones the signature's font draws, or the call is refused naming the label and character. PAdES B-B, SHA-256 (SHA-384 for P-384 keys).

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `id` * | string | Digital ID file (.p12 / .pfx), keychain: reference on macOS, or windows: reference on Windows. |
| `out` * | string | Where to save the signed document. |
| `appearance` | object | What a visible signature shows; items not given keep their default. |
| `certify` | enum: no_changes, form_fill, comments |  |
| `contact` | string |  |
| `field` | string |  |
| `graphic` | object | Exactly one of image, text or strokes. |
| `labels` | object | The words of a visible signature's labels (at most 200 characters each, Western European characters only); labels not given stay English. |
| `location` | string |  |
| `page` | integer |  |
| `password` | string |  |
| `reason` | string |  |
| `rect` | array |  |

## `text_edit`

**Edit text**

Replace the text of one paragraph (paragraph, from text_paragraphs: rewrapped to the paragraph's width with its line spacing) or one line (line, from text_lines) in place, keeping position, size and colour. For a mixed-style region, editor_text supplies visual row breaks; surviving text keeps its source-run styles and inserted text inherits the surrounding run. For a paragraph, also change its formatting: font (helvetica, times, courier) with bold/italic, size (points), color (#rrggbb), align (left, center, right, justify), underline, line_spacing (× size), char_spacing (points) and scale (horizontal, percent), or move it (dx, dy in points; up is +dy) and rewrap it to a new width (points); text may then be omitted. Its own font is reused when it can show every character and no font/weight change is requested; otherwise it uses a standard font matching the source style or, for text no standard font can show, real fallback outlines from PdfCraft's own faces, from the one that has every character: the craft-fonts Japanese faces (Mincho/Gothic matching the requested/source family and available weight) or, behind them, the bundled Inter face, which carries the Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters they lack (Uzbek қ, Kazakh ә). The result shows the font used, and for a paragraph its text unless the document's security doesn't allow copying. Missing Japanese weights use Regular, not synthetic bold; the small web build has only Gothic Regular. Paragraph bold may be set without font to keep the source family. Text that no available font can show is refused. A paragraph number is refused when an earlier edit merged that paragraph into a neighbour (list the page again); the result's stale_paragraphs names the numbers gone. Undoable.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `page` * | integer |  |
| `align` | enum: left, center, right, justify |  |
| `aligns` | array | Each paragraph's (line's) own alignment, by index; inherit (or legacy null) follows align. |
| `bold` | boolean |  |
| `char_spacing` | number | Points. |
| `color` | string | #rrggbb |
| `dx` | number | Paragraph only: move right by this many points (negative: left). |
| `dy` | number | Paragraph only: move up by this many points (negative: down). |
| `font` | enum: helvetica, times, courier |  |
| `font_resource` | string | Explicit source/full page font resource from text_fonts or text_font_import. |
| `italic` | boolean |  |
| `line` | integer |  |
| `line_spacing` | number | Multiple of the font size (1.2 is ordinary). |
| `paragraph` | integer |  |
| `ranges` | array | Disjoint UTF-8 byte ranges in replacement text; unspecified source formatting survives. |
| `scale` | number | Horizontal scale in percent. |
| `size` | number |  |
| `text` | string |  |
| `underline` | boolean |  |
| `width` | number | Paragraph only: rewrap to this width in points (dragging the box's edge). |

**Extract text**  _(read-only)_

Extract the text of some or all pages, in reading order. With rect, only the text inside that rectangle on each page, as Column select takes it: one row per visual line, side-by-side pieces (table cells) separated by a tab.

## `text_find`

**Find text**  _(read-only)_

Find a phrase (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalised) and return matches in page order with page and line rectangles in points (origin top-left). Reads growing batches, looking one match past the limit for a continuation. Failed pages do not discard readable matches: warnings contains up to 100 {page, error, error_truncated} entries (errors capped at 1024 UTF-8 bytes), warning_count counts failed pages, and warnings_truncated reports a capped list. complete is false after a page failure or when more matches exist; next is present only for a match-limit continuation.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `query` * | string |  |
| `limit` | integer | Maximum matches (default 500). When another match exists, next holds start_page and skip to continue. complete is false for either additional matches or failed pages; an exhausted search with warnings has no next. |
| `skip` | integer | Matches to pass over on start_page before returning any (default 0). |
| `start_page` | integer | Page to start searching from (default 1). |

The scan skips symlinks, collections and invalid/licence-restricted fonts, with depth, entry and byte budgets. Select a returned path with text_font_import.

No system-interface fallback is exported.

## `text_script`

**Superscript or subscript**

Format text ▸ Superscript or Subscript on one paragraph (paragraph, from text_paragraphs), or on range [start, end): UTF-8 byte offsets of its editor_text. The characters take the Unicode superscript or subscript forms (2 → ², 2 → ₂; the font must have those glyphs, and extracted text contains them); text already in that script goes back to plain characters. Characters Unicode has no such form for (q, a space) stay unchanged and do not determine the selection's script state. Mixed plain and target-script characters normalize to that script, then to plain text on the next call (H₂2 → H₂₂ → H22); a second toggle does not reconstruct the original mixture. Use Undo to restore the exact prior text. The paragraph is then rewritten as text_edit rewrites it, with the same result fields. Refused when no character would change. Undoable. Mathematical minus U+2212 has its own script mapping; ASCII hyphen-minus stays unchanged.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `page` * | integer |  |
| `paragraph` * | integer |  |
| `script` * | enum: superscript, subscript |  |
| `range` | array | UTF-8 byte offsets [start, end) of the paragraph's editor_text; the whole paragraph when omitted. |

Image exclusion removes Figure-tagged and invisible/OCR text. Does not run OCR. Copy permission is required. Fails rather than returning a partial total when a page cannot be read.

## `view_reading_colors`

**Set reading colours**

Set the document's reading colours (Acrobat's Replace Document Colors, in the Reading Options): solid text and line-art paints are remapped for readability and the page clears to the background colour in page_render. A view setting: the file doesn't change. mode is one of: off, black-on-white, white-on-black, yellow-on-black, green-on-black, or custom (which takes text and background as #RRGGBB). only_black maps only near-black paints (default false) and line_art also maps line-art paints (default true); both override the mode's preset. A flag that differs from the mode's preset default makes the returned mode read custom, because the resulting params no longer match any preset. Returns the resulting setting.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
| `mode` * | enum: off, black-on-white, white-on-black, yellow-on-black, green-on-black, custom |  |
| `background` | string | With mode custom: the background colour, #RRGGBB. |
| `line_art` | boolean | Also map line-art paints. Default true. |
| `only_black` | boolean | Map only near-black paints. Default false. |
| `text` | string | With mode custom: the text colour, #RRGGBB. |

**Convert an XFA form to a static form**

Make an XFA form an ordinary PDF form: the XFA packets (template, data, scripts) and PdfCraft's private keys go; the pages as laid out and the fields with their values stay, so every viewer shows the same form and none lays it out again. Its scripts no longer run. Undoable until saved.

| argument | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` * | integer | Document id from doc_open or doc_list. |
